title: Call to Arms (Nahan), including the 'Iron House' preface

access.edition_or_version: First collection, 1923 (later English translations; translation copyright varies)
access.translator: Not fixed; translation consulted only at reference level

mechanics.premise: A landmark modern Chinese story collection whose preface uses the 'iron house' image: a small number of awake people in an inescapable house, wondering whether to wake the sleepers.
mechanics.tone_function: A non-Anglophone model of urgency as anguished responsibility: the reader is asked whether silence before catastrophe is defensible.
mechanics.time_handling: The image makes the present the last available moment; urgency is existential and national rather than commercial.
mechanics.figurative_moves: Sustained allegory (the sealed house, the sleepers, the fire) carries the pressure; the metaphor does the argumentative work.
mechanics.rhetorical_position: Conditional, self-questioning voice rather than command; urgency rises from moral dilemma, not imperative volume.
mechanics.cultural_scope: Chinese vernacular-modernist reform context, distinct from Western deadline rhetoric; no false universal claim is made.
mechanics.translation_limits: Chinese prose style and sound are not assessed; the iron-house preface is summarized from established descriptions, not from a fixed translation.
mechanics.verification_note: Lu Xun and the collection confirmed via reference summary; the preface's iron-house image described, not quoted. Marked partial because no single translation edition was page-inspected.
